patterns.name: Hidden Mint Function
patterns.description: Owner-only function that can mint unlimited tokens, diluting holders
patterns.recommendation: Remove owner-only mint capability or add a hard cap enforced in the contract

patterns.name: Unlimited Mint Without Cap
patterns.description: Mint function with no supply cap check — can inflate token supply infinitely
patterns.recommendation: Add a maximum supply check before any mint operation

patterns.name: Owner Can Pause Transfers
patterns.description: Owner can freeze all token transfers, trapping user funds
patterns.recommendation: If pause is needed, add a timelock or multi-sig requirement

patterns.name: Blacklist Function
patterns.description: Owner can blacklist addresses, preventing them from transferring tokens
patterns.recommendation: Remove blacklist capability or require governance/multi-sig approval

patterns.name: Hidden Fee Modification
patterns.description: Owner can change transaction fees to any value, potentially setting 100% fee
patterns.recommendation: Add a maximum fee cap (e.g., 10%) enforced in the setter function

patterns.name: Drain Function
patterns.description: Function that can withdraw all ETH or tokens from the contract to the owner
patterns.recommendation: Remove arbitrary fund withdrawal or add timelock with public notice period

patterns.name: Self-Destruct Capability
patterns.description: Contract can be destroyed by owner, potentially stealing all funds
patterns.recommendation: Remove selfdestruct — it is deprecated and extremely dangerous

patterns.name: Hidden Transfer to Owner in Fees
patterns.description: Transfer function silently sends a portion of every transaction to owner/dev wallet
patterns.recommendation: Make all fee recipients transparent and immutable, or use a fee distribution contract

patterns.name: Upgradeable Proxy Without Timelock
patterns.description: Proxy pattern allows owner to swap implementation instantly, potentially inserting malicious code
patterns.recommendation: Add a timelock (e.g., 48h) with public announcement before upgrades take effect

patterns.name: Delegatecall to Arbitrary Address
patterns.description: delegatecall with a user-controlled or owner-controlled target can execute any code
patterns.recommendation: Never delegatecall to an address that can be changed by an admin without a timelock

patterns.name: Hidden External Call
patterns.description: Low-level call to an address stored in a mutable state variable
patterns.recommendation: Verify the target address is immutable or governed by a timelock

patterns.name: Approval Manipulation
patterns.description: Contract can approve unlimited token spending on behalf of users
patterns.recommendation: Only approve the exact amount needed, never unlimited

patterns.name: Hidden Admin Role
patterns.description: Multiple admin-like roles that can perform privileged operations
patterns.recommendation: Document all admin roles. Ensure they are governed by multi-sig or DAO

patterns.name: Assembly with Arbitrary Memory Access
patterns.description: Inline assembly can bypass Solidity safety checks and hide malicious operations
patterns.recommendation: Audit all assembly blocks. Prefer Solidity equivalents where possible

patterns.name: Manipulable Oracle
patterns.description: Price or data oracle can be set by owner to any value
patterns.recommendation: Use decentralized oracles (Chainlink). If custom, add timelock on oracle changes

patterns.name: Reentrancy Risk
patterns.description: External call before state update — classic reentrancy pattern
patterns.recommendation: Use checks-effects-interactions pattern or OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard

patterns.name: tx.origin Authentication
patterns.description: Using tx.origin for auth is vulnerable to phishing attacks
patterns.recommendation: Use msg.sender instead of tx.origin for authentication

patterns.name: Unchecked Return Value
patterns.description: Return value of external call not checked — funds may silently fail to send
patterns.recommendation: Always check the return value of low-level calls

patterns.name: Timestamp Dependence
patterns.description: Using block.timestamp for critical logic — miners can manipulate within ~15s
patterns.recommendation: Avoid using block.timestamp for precise timing. Use block numbers or oracles

patterns.name: Unsafe CoreWriter Order Placement
patterns.description: Placing orders via CoreWriter precompile without proper slippage or size validation
patterns.recommendation: Validate order parameters and add slippage protection before CoreWriter calls

patterns.name: Unprotected HyperCore Bridge Transfer
patterns.description: Bridging assets between HyperEVM and HyperCore without validation
patterns.recommendation: Add proper access control and validation for cross-environment transfers

patterns.name: MEV Vulnerability in Order Flow
patterns.description: Order placement pattern susceptible to front-running or sandwich attacks
patterns.recommendation: Add deadline and slippage protection to all order submissions

patterns.name: Unbounded Liquidation Exposure
patterns.description: Leveraged position without proper margin or stop-loss checks
patterns.recommendation: Add maximum leverage limits and automated stop-loss mechanisms
